title: Learning Model Demos
one_liner: Interactive demos of classic associative learning models, starting with Rescorla-Wagner and Mackintosh and leading up to MINERVA-AL, so people can run each model and see how it learns.
description:
## What

Example demos that show how learning models work. They begin with classic models such as Rescorla-Wagner and Mackintosh and build toward MINERVA-AL, the instance-based model of associative learning.

## Why

Learning models are much easier to understand when you can run them. Watching associative strength change trial by trial makes each model's assumptions concrete. Running the same training design through several models shows where they agree and where they make different predictions. Ending with MINERVA-AL shows how an instance-based account handles the same phenomena in a different way.

## How

Early thoughts, to refine in a workshop:

- **A sequence of models.** Rescorla-Wagner first, then Mackintosh's attention model, possibly Pearce-Hall and a configural model, and then MINERVA-AL.
- **Interactive in the browser.** Each demo lets people set learning parameters, design a sequence of trials, run it, and watch the predictions change over trials on a chart.
- **Classic phenomena as presets.** Acquisition, extinction, blocking, overshadowing, conditioned inhibition, latent inhibition, backward blocking, and negative patterning. Several of these are exactly where the models part ways, which makes them good teaching cases.
- **Side by side.** Run one design through two or more models at once to compare their predictions directly.
- **Show the equations.** Pair each model with its update rule or retrieval equations, with the live values highlighted as trials run.
- **Simple to host.** Plain HTML and JavaScript, so the demos run anywhere and could be deployed on Coolify or the lab website. Matching R or Quarto versions could support course materials.
- **Connections.** Useful for teaching and for classroom demos on the Open Psychology Platform. A good example of how computational models make predictions explicit, the theme of the theory-evaluation idea. A lead-in to the instance theory work, including the ITS experiments.
